checklist.label: Atrophy
checklist.detail: Describe global and regional volume loss, symmetry and age context.

checklist.label: Medial temporal structures
checklist.detail: Assess both hippocampi on comparable coronal planes.

checklist.label: Vascular burden
checklist.detail: Record white-matter disease, lacunes, strategic and territorial infarcts.

checklist.label: Blood products
checklist.detail: Describe microbleed count/distribution and cortical superficial siderosis.

checklist.label: Treatable mimics
checklist.detail: Exclude mass, hydrocephalus, collection and acute diffusion abnormality.

measurements.name: MTA score
measurements.method: Report right and left 0–4 visual scores on standard coronal T1 planes.
measurements.pitfall: Interpret with age and clinical phenotype; MTA is not specific for Alzheimer disease.

measurements.name: Fazekas score
measurements.method: Record deep/periventricular white-matter burden using the stated visual scale.
measurements.pitfall: FLAIR intensity alone does not establish vascular aetiology.

measurements.name: Microbleeds
measurements.method: Count or describe burden and lobar/deep/infratentorial distribution on the same susceptibility technique.
measurements.pitfall: Different field strength or sequence sensitivity can mimic interval increase.

classification.name: Visual atrophy and white-matter scales
classification.version: MTA 0–4; Fazekas 0–3; name any additional scale
classification.applicability: Descriptive structural MRI assessment in cognitive impairment.
classification.summary: Report individual scores and their anatomic context. They describe burden and pattern; they do not replace clinical diagnosis or biomarker assessment.

pitfalls: An atrophy pattern supports a differential; it does not independently diagnose dementia subtype.
Rapidly progressive symptoms require a different differential even when atrophy is present.
impression_prompts: Is atrophy disproportionate for age, and what is its distribution?
What is the cerebrovascular and haemorrhagic burden?
Is there a structural alternative or urgent finding?
escalation: Escalate acute infarction, mass effect or unexpected rapid-progressive diffusion abnormalities in the clinical context.

steps.label: Global and regional atrophy
steps.detail: Describe global cortical atrophy and any regional predominance, symmetry and age appropriateness.
findings: Global cortical atrophy, GCA [2].
Asymmetric frontal and anterior temporal atrophy (frontotemporal lobar degeneration pattern).
Posterior parietal and precuneus atrophy (Koedam [2]).
steps.look: Axial FLAIR and 3D T1 in three planes; GCA scale 0–3; posterior atrophy (Koedam) on sagittal and coronal images.

steps.label: Medial temporal lobe atrophy
steps.detail: Assess both hippocampi on comparable coronal planes with the MTA score.
findings: MTA right __/4, left __/4 (abnormal for age).
Asymmetric hippocampal atrophy, [left] greater than [right].
steps.look: Coronal T1 through the hippocampal body at the level of the pons.
steps.tip: An MTA score of 2 or more under 75 years, or 3 or more at 75 and above, is usually considered abnormal.

steps.label: Vascular burden
steps.detail: Record white-matter disease (Fazekas), lacunes and strategic or territorial infarcts.

normal.SMALL-VESSEL AND ISCHAEMIC DISEASE: No significant white-matter disease (Fazekas 0–1); no infarcts.

findings: Confluent white-matter hyperintensities, Fazekas 3.
Lacunes in the basal ganglia and thalami.
Strategic infarct in the [left thalamus].
steps.look: FLAIR for white-matter lesions and lacunes; strategic sites: thalamus, caudate, angular gyrus.

steps.label: Microbleeds and siderosis
steps.detail: Describe microbleed number and distribution and cortical superficial siderosis.
findings: __ lobar microbleeds with cortical superficial siderosis (cerebral amyloid angiopathy pattern).
Deep microbleeds in the basal ganglia and pons (hypertensive pattern).
steps.tip: Lobar microbleeds and superficial siderosis suggest amyloid angiopathy and matter for anti-amyloid treatment eligibility.

steps.label: Treatable and alternative causes
steps.detail: Exclude mass, subdural collection, hydrocephalus, acute diffusion abnormality and other structural causes.

normal.ALTERNATIVE STRUCTURAL CAUSES: No mass, collection, hydrocephalus or diffusion abnormality.

findings: Ventriculomegaly disproportionate to sulcal widening with tight high-convexity sulci (normal pressure hydrocephalus pattern).
Cortical ribbon and deep grey diffusion restriction (Creutzfeldt–Jakob disease pattern).
Chronic subdural haematoma.
steps.look: DWI for cortical ribbon and deep grey restriction; ventricles versus sulci; subdural spaces.
steps.tip: Rapidly progressive symptoms need a different differential, including Creutzfeldt–Jakob disease.

protocol: Use HARNESS structural sequences: isotropic 3D T1, isotropic 3D FLAIR and high-resolution coronal T2 perpendicular to the hippocampal long axis; add sequences for the clinical question.
Review seizure semiology, EEG localisation and timing of recent seizures; consider age-related myelination when adapting paediatric protocols.

checklist.label: Hippocampi
checklist.detail: Compare size, signal, internal architecture and orientation bilaterally.

checklist.label: Cortical development
checklist.detail: Inspect thickness, sulcation, grey-white junction and transmantle signal.

checklist.label: Dual pathology
checklist.detail: Search the entire brain even after detecting hippocampal sclerosis.

checklist.label: Other substrates
checklist.detail: Assess tumour, vascular malformation, gliosis, encephalomalacia and encephalocele.

checklist.label: Concordance
checklist.detail: Describe lesion location relative to supplied electroclinical localisation without inferring causality.

measurements.name: Lesion dimensions
measurements.method: Measure a suspected epileptogenic structural lesion in three planes and identify sequences.
measurements.pitfall: Transient peri-ictal swelling can alter apparent extent.

measurements.name: Hippocampal asymmetry
measurements.method: Use visual comparison or validated volumetry with age-appropriate reference data.
measurements.pitfall: Oblique planes and segmentation errors can create false asymmetry.

classification.name: HARNESS-MRI
classification.applicability: Dedicated structural epilepsy MRI; adapt for infants and specific clinical questions.
classification.summary: A standard acquisition protocol, not a diagnostic severity score. A normal study does not exclude epilepsy.

pitfalls: Normal MRI does not exclude epilepsy or subtle focal cortical dysplasia.
Peri-ictal diffusion and FLAIR change may be reversible; use the clinical timeline.
impression_prompts: Is there a structural lesion plausibly relevant to seizures?
Which side/region and associated second lesion are involved?
Is the examination adequate or is targeted expert review warranted?
escalation: Communicate acute haemorrhage, infarction, encephalitis pattern or a mass with threatening pressure effect.

steps.label: Hippocampi
steps.detail: Compare hippocampal size, signal and internal architecture bilaterally.

normal.MESIAL TEMPORAL STRUCTURES: Hippocampi symmetric with normal size, signal and internal architecture.

findings: [Left] hippocampal sclerosis: volume loss, increased T2/FLAIR signal and loss of internal architecture.
Atrophy of the ipsilateral fornix and mammillary body.
steps.look: High-resolution coronal T2 perpendicular to the hippocampal long axis; 3D FLAIR.
steps.tip: Look at the whole brain even after finding hippocampal sclerosis: dual pathology is common.

steps.label: Cortex and neuronal migration
steps.detail: Inspect cortical thickness, sulcation, grey–white junction, heterotopia and transmantle signal.

normal.CORTEX AND MIGRATION: Normal cortical thickness and grey–white junction; no heterotopia.

findings: Blurring of the grey–white junction with cortical thickening and a transmantle sign in the [right] [frontal] lobe (focal cortical dysplasia type II pattern).
Subependymal nodular heterotopia along the [ ] ventricle.
Polymicrogyria of the [ ].
steps.look: 3D T1 and 3D FLAIR in all planes; compare with the other hemisphere.
steps.tip: A funnel-shaped T2/FLAIR abnormality extending from the cortex towards the ventricle supports focal cortical dysplasia type II, most often IIb; imaging does not establish the histological subtype.

steps.label: Focal lesions
steps.detail: Look for tumours, vascular malformations, gliosis and encephalomalacia.

normal.FOCAL LESIONS: No tumour, vascular malformation or gliosis.

findings: Cavernoma __ mm in the [ ] with a haemosiderin rim.
Cortically based cystic lesion (DNET / ganglioglioma pattern).
Post-traumatic encephalomalacia and gliosis in the [ ].
steps.look: Susceptibility images for cavernomas; post-contrast images when acquired.

steps.label: Temporal encephalocele and dual pathology
steps.detail: Look for temporal encephalocele, prior injury and any second relevant lesion.
findings: Temporal pole encephalocele through a middle cranial fossa defect.
Second lesion: [ ] in addition to hippocampal sclerosis.
steps.look: Coronal and sagittal images of the middle cranial fossa floor.

steps.label: Electroclinical concordance
steps.detail: Relate the lesion to the supplied EEG and semiology localisation without assuming causality, and consider peri-ictal change.

normal.ACUTE AND ELECTROCLINICAL CORRELATION: No peri-ictal change. No structural lesion; this does not exclude epilepsy.

findings: Lesion concordant with the supplied [left temporal] EEG focus.
Transient cortical and hippocampal diffusion and FLAIR change, compatible with peri-ictal change; follow-up to confirm resolution.
steps.look: Supplied EEG and semiology; the timing of the last seizure.
steps.tip: A normal MRI does not exclude epilepsy or subtle focal cortical dysplasia.
